evidence.summary: Pi's core agent loop lives in the standalone workspace package `packages/agent` (the docs label it "Agent loop and message types"); it is NOT under `packages/coding-agent/src/agent`, which does not exist. The low-level loop is in `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts`: `runLoop()` drives an outer follow-up loop wrapping an inner turn loop. Each turn streams one assistant message (`streamAssistantResponse`), filters its content for `toolCall` parts, executes them (parallel by default, sequential if configured or if any invoked tool is `executionMode: "sequential"`), pushes the resulting `toolResult` messages back into BOTH the live LLM context and the returned `newMessages` transcript, and emits lifecycle events (`agent_start`, `turn_start`, `message_start/update/end`, `tool_execution_start/update/end`, `turn_end`, `agent_end`). The loop continues while `hasMoreToolCalls || pendingMessages.length > 0`. Stop conditions: (1) assistant `stopReason === "error" || "aborted"` -> immediate agent_end; (2) every finalized tool result in a batch has `result.terminate === true` (early termination); (3) the optional `config.shouldStopAfterTurn(...)` hook returns truthy; (4) natural exit when there are no tool calls and no steering/follow-up messages queued. There is NO built-in numeric `max_turns` cap and no `no_tool_calls` named constant in the loop. Abort is cooperative via an `AbortSignal` checked in tool prep and between tool executions and forwarded to the stream function; the stateful `Agent` class (`agent.ts`) owns the `AbortController`, transcript, steering/follow-up queues, and lifecycle, and is what the coding-agent CLI wraps via `core/agent-session.ts`.

evidence.summary: Pi's coding-agent ships seven built-in tools — read, bash, edit, write, grep, find, ls — each defined in its own file under packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/ using TypeBox schemas, and assembled by factory functions in tools/index.ts (createCodingTools = read+bash+edit+write; createReadOnlyTools = read+grep+find+ls; createAllTools = all seven). CLI flags --tools/-t, --exclude-tools/-xt, --no-builtin-tools/-nbt and --no-tools/-nt select the active set, with builtinToolsList hardcoded to the same seven names in cli/args.ts. There is NO core allow/ask/block permission engine: docs/usage.md explicitly says Pi omits "permission popups", and gating is implemented as an extension via the "tool_call" event whose handler returns ToolCallEventResult { block?: boolean; reason?: string } (the only built-in decision is block-or-not). The shipped example extension permission-gate.ts demonstrates this: it pattern-matches dangerous bash commands and returns { block: true, reason } (default-blocking when no UI), or undefined to allow.

evidence.summary: Skills are self-contained, on-demand capability packages: a directory with a SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter + Markdown) plus freeform scripts/references/assets. Pi implements the Agent Skills standard (agentskills.io) leniently: most violations emit warning diagnostics but the skill still loads; only a missing/empty description blocks loading. The implementation lives in packages/coding-agent/src/core/skills.ts (loadSkills/loadSkillsFromDir/loadSkillFromFile/formatSkillsForPrompt). Progressive disclosure is real: only name+description+location are emitted into the system prompt as <available_skills> XML; the full SKILL.md is loaded on demand via the read tool or the /skill:name command. Same-name collisions keep the FIRST skill found (Map-based) and emit a collision diagnostic. Note: the doc's broad discovery-source list (packages/package.json pi.skills, settings skills array, CLI --skill) is wider than what core/skills.ts itself implements — loadSkills() only auto-includes the user (~/.pi/agent/skills) and project (.pi/skills) default dirs plus an explicit skillPaths list; the other sources are wired upstream of this module.

evidence.summary: Pi persists each conversation as an append-only JSONL session file with a tree structure: every entry carries an id and parentId, and a "leaf" pointer marks the current position; appending creates a child of the leaf and branching just moves the leaf (see SessionManager class doc comment, session-manager.ts:730-740). On top of this tree sit five user-facing branching/continuation commands registered in core/slash-commands.ts: /resume (open a different session via picker), /tree (navigate/switch branches in the same file), /fork (new session file starting from an earlier user message), /clone (new session file duplicating the current leaf position), and /compact (summarize older context, optional custom prompt). /tree edits in place while /fork and /clone create new session files. The SessionManager (packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts) provides the underlying primitives: branch(), branchWithSummary(), createBranchedSession(), forkFrom(), continueRecent(), open(), and newSession({parentSession}).

evidence.summary: Pi persists each agent session as an append-only JSONL file: the first line is a SessionHeader (type:"session") and each subsequent line is a SessionEntry. Entries form a tree via id (8 hex chars) and parentId (string|null), so divergent conversation paths live in one file ("in-place branching"); a private leafId marks the current position and appends attach as children of that leaf. Files live under <agentDir>/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/<isoTimestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl where agentDir is ~/.pi/agent (homedir + CONFIG_DIR_NAME ".pi" + "agent"). The header has a version field; CURRENT_SESSION_VERSION = 3, and v1 (linear) and v2 (tree) sessions are migrated in place on load (v1->v2 adds id/parentId; v2->v3 renames the hookMessage role to custom). Entry discriminators: message, thinking_level_change, model_change, compaction, branch_summary, custom, custom_message, label, session_info. The canonical types and the SessionManager class live in packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts; there is no src/session directory.

evidence.summary: Prompt templates in Pi are Markdown files (optionally with YAML frontmatter) that expand into full prompts; you invoke one by typing /name where name is the filename minus .md. The coding-agent implementation lives in packages/coding-agent/src/core/prompt-templates.ts (self-contained: filesystem loader + arg parser + substitution), and a parallel, env-abstracted implementation lives in packages/agent/src/harness/prompt-templates.ts (used by the lower-level agent harness). Frontmatter is parsed for `description` and `argument-hint`; description falls back to the first non-empty body line truncated to 60 chars. Argument substitution is bash-style: $1..$N positional (replaced FIRST), ${@:N} / ${@:N:L} 1-indexed slices, then $ARGUMENTS and $@ (all args joined by a space). Loading is non-recursive over .md files; defaults come from agentDir/prompts (global) and cwd/.pi/prompts (project), plus explicit --prompt-template paths. The doc-claimed source dir src/prompts does NOT exist.

evidence.summary: Pi's provider system supports three credential mechanisms: OAuth subscription logins, explicit API-key providers (env var or auth file), and cloud/ambient-credential providers (Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, Cloudflare AI Gateway/Workers AI, Google Vertex AI). There are exactly three built-in OAuth providers, registered in OAUTH_PROVIDERS in packages/ai/src/utils/oauth/index.ts: anthropic (Claude Pro/Max), github-copilot, and openai-codex (ChatGPT Plus/Pro). A package is an npm-style directory whose package.json carries a `pi` manifest key declaring resource arrays (extensions/skills/prompts/themes), or it relies on convention directories (extensions/, skills/, prompts/, themes/). evidence.summary: Pi's coding-agent exposes two non-TUI host-driving output modes selected by --mode. RPC mode (src/modes/rpc/, started via `pi --mode rpc`) is a bidirectional headless protocol: the host writes JSON command objects to stdin (one per line) and reads back `response` objects (echoing an optional correlation `id`) plus a stream of agent events. JSON mode (`--mode json`, also reachable via `--print`/`-p`) emits the agent's event stream as JSON Lines to stdout for scripting. Both modes serialize each record as one JSON object per LF-delimited line; RPC additionally parses stdin with strict JSONL semantics (split on \n only, strip an optional trailing \r), deliberately avoiding Node `readline` which would also split on U+2028/U+2029. Note: the prompt's named primary doc /packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc.md exists and was read in full; the named source dir src/sdk does NOT exist (sources live in src/modes/rpc and src/modes/print-mode.ts).
